Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prod degradation — initial timeline and impact (Acme AI)

Quick note to loop leadership in — we had a service degradation affecting hosted text-generation endpoints that impacted a subset of Acme AI traffic between 2026-06-20T08:20Z and 2026-06-20T09:05Z (roughly 45 minutes).

What we know so far:
- Symptom: elevated p95/p99 latencies and a 4.6% error spike on the katana-prod cluster. Customer-facing errors were 502/504 for long-context requests.
- Preliminary SLA impact: estimated 1.2% monthly SLA breach for Acme AI's bucket (based on token-weighted request distribution).
- Mitigation applied: scaled dedicated pool + temporary routing to fallback model variant at 08:50Z; errors subsided by 09:05Z.

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (initial timeline export).

Action items I'm starting: capture full timeline, correlate autoscaler events, collect driver/kernel logs from affected hosts. Rishi, can you own the RCA draft? Laura, we need customer-facing language and a recommended credit if we confirm the SLA exposure. Vivek, requesting exec one-paragraph summary for QBR materials by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Subject: RCA draft: autoscaler threshold + driver GC interaction (for review)

Draft RCA (please review and flag edits):
Root cause (summary): An autoscaler edge-case combined with a GPU driver memory-management GC introduced a transient backlog for long-context requests. Specifically, an incorrect threshold in the horizontal autoscaler caused a 30s delay in scale decisions under a burst pattern, while a sporadic driver-side GC event increased per-request latency for large KV-cache allocations. When these two correlated, the request queue grew and the frontend returned 502/504 for timed-out requests.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:18Z: sustained burst from Acme AI (long-context generation).
- 08:25Z: driver GC spikes observed on host group katana-03/katana-04.
- 08:28Z: autoscaler evaluated but missed the latency signal due to incorrect metric window (configured for 60s vs expected 30s).
- 08:50Z: mitigation: manual scale + routing to fallback model variant.
- 09:05Z: metrics returned to baseline.

Customer impact: estimated 45 minutes of partial availability for 12% of Acme AI requests in that interval; token-weighted exposure maps to ~1.2% of their monthly SLA allocation.

Remediations completed / in-flight:
- Immediate: autoscaler metric window fixed and pushed (deployed 2026-06-22).
- Immediate: hotpatch to GPU driver allocation knob to reduce GC pressure (applied 2026-06-22).
- Short term: add targeted CI test for long-context KV allocations (owner: infra-team, due 2026-07-10).
- Mid term: replace autoscaler metric evaluation engine with event-driven signal (owner: rishi.malhotra, due 2026-08-01).

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Finalize RCA doc and produce one-slide exec summary — owner: rishi.malhotra — ETA: 2026-06-24 EOD.
2) Customer-facing note (plain language) + recommended SLA credit — owner: laura.bennett — ETA: 2026-06-25.
3) Add automated alert for driver-GC anomalies — owner: infra-sre — ETA: 2026-07-05.
4) Add long-context performance test into nightly regression suite — owner: qa-team — ETA: 2026-07-12.

Attachments: rca-draft.md

Subject: Exec-facing summary + SLA credit recommendation (Acme AI)

Folks — I've drafted the customer-facing summary and a recommended credit. Please review and sign off so we can send this during the QBR.

Executive summary (one paragraph): On 2026-06-20 we experienced a short-lived service degradation that affected long-context generation for a subset of Acme AI traffic. The issue was caused by a correlated autoscaler threshold configuration and sporadic GPU-driver GC events that together caused request queuing and timeouts; mitigation included manual scaling and routing to a fallback model. We've applied a hotfix to the autoscaler configuration and a driver allocation adjustment; longer-term fixes and testing are in progress.

Customer-facing ask / recommended credit: Given the confirmed exposure (~1.2% of monthly SLA allocation for the affected customer bucket) and the visibility of the failure mode, I recommend offering a 10% credit of their affected month invoice as a good-faith gesture and to preserve the relationship. This aligns with our standard playbook for partial monthly SLA exposure.

Attachments: exec-summary-for-qbr.docx (1-page wording to read at QBR), qbr-slide-deck-v2.pptx (updated slide with graph placeholders).

Tara / Procurement: we'll plan to present the situation and the credit recommendation at the scheduled QBR unless you prefer a pre-QBR call.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success
